The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[-4,2].$ The graph of ${f}^{′}(x)$, the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above, where the areas of the regions between the graph and the $x$-axis are $4$ and $2,$ respectively (from left to right).

Given that $f(2)=-3,$ what is the maximum value ${f}_{\text{max}}$ of $f(x)$ on the interval $[-4,2]?$

${f}_{\text{max}}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
According to the candidates test, the maximum value of $f(x)$ on $[-4,2]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval.

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (-4,2),$ and ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at $x=-1.$ Therefore, the candidates are $x=-4,-1,2.$

**Step 2**: Compute the value of $f$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

Using the given information and the fundamental theorem of calculus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) & =-3 \\ f(-1) & =f(2)+{\int }_{2}^{-1}{f}^{′}(t)\,dt \\  & =f(2)-{\int }_{-1}^{2}{f}^{′}(t)\,dt \\  & =-3-(-2) \\  & =-1 \\ f(-4) & =f(2)+{\int }_{2}^{-4}{f}^{′}(t)\,dt \\  & =f(2)-{\int }_{-4}^{2}{f}^{′}(t)\,dt \\  & =-3-(4+(-2)) \\  & =-3-2 \\  & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the largest value of $f$ from our candidates.

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{f}_{\text{max}}=max\{-3,-1,-5\}=-1.
$$

Therefore, the maximum value of $f$ is ${f}_{\text{max}}=-1,$ and the value of $x$ that maximizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{max}}=-1.$
